stem: A logistics company's order-entry application runs entirely in the eu-west-1 Region, but a new backend service the team is building will run in the us-east-1 Region and will query the same order database heavily. The team wants to minimize the extra network latency the new service will experience. Which TWO actions help? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Deploy the new backend service in the eu-west-1 Region alongside the database instead of us-east-1
Increase the primary database's provisioned IOPS
Create a cross-Region read replica in us-east-1 for the new service's read queries
Turn on RDS storage auto scaling for the primary database instance
Create an additional read replica in the eu-west-1 Region for the new service's queries

rationale: Keeping the new service in the same Region as the database removes the cross-Region hop entirely, and a replica placed in us-east-1 gives the service a local copy to read from instead of crossing Regions on every query. Increasing provisioned IOPS and enabling storage auto scaling both improve the primary's own I/O performance but do nothing about the distance the new service's traffic must travel. A replica placed back in eu-west-1 sits exactly as far from a us-east-1 service as the primary does, so it does not shorten that path either.
